full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs case in short, is that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 101 of 1974 was fraudulent, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaint case is that defendant No. 1 filed the aforesaid Title Suit No. 101 of 1974 against Amulya Prashad Ghose, husband of the present plaintiff and by suppressing the summons and notices of the said suit and by filing a forged, fraudulent and collusive solenama got compromise decree for specific performance of contract. Her further case is that her husband Amulya Prashad did not appear in the aforesaid suit and did not execute any solenama or any vokalatnama and the signatures on the solenama and vokalatnama are all forged and fabricated. Defendant No. 1 who was plaintiff in Title Suit No. 101 of 1974 contested the suit contending, inter alia, that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 101 of 1974 is not fraudulent and void. The defendant's positive case is that, in that suit Amulya Prashad himself appeared and filed the solenama and the decree was passed after due service of sumons and no fraud was practised either upon the Court or upon the defendant of that suit. 

 3. The trial Judge dismissed the suit by holding that the solenama passed in the earlier  suit was a genuine one. On appeal, the lower appellate Court decreed the suit by holding that no summons were served upon the defendant of that suit and that the solenama was a forged and fabricated document. The High Court Division in revision set aside the appellate judgment and decree and dismissed the suit. 

 7. At the outset, it is to be stated that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division did not himself compare the signatures purported to be of Amulya Prashad on the vokalatnama and solenama of title Suit No. 101 of 1974 with the admitted signature of Amulya on the plaint of the present suit. 

 8. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has, of course, elaborately dealt in his judgment with regard to the question of comparison of the disputed signatures or writings with the admitted writings as contemplated under Section 73 of the Evidence Act. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, while considering the question as to the genuineness of the impugned solenama, on the basis of which the impugned decree was passed himself, of course, without comparing the disputed signatures held that such comparison is hazardous and not free from errors. We like to mention here that law prescribes for such comparison of signatures or writings. Further, whether this method is inconclusive or hazardous can only be opined in the fact of a case, provided the same is compared by the Court itself. Since, in the present case, the Single Judge of the High Court Division has not done so, his approach was totally illegal and erroneous. 

 9. Herein below we will refer to the findings of the lower appellate Court on the question of comparison of disputed signatures as found by the lower appellate Court. In the present case, the signatures were not sent to the hand-writing expert for opinion and as a matter of fact there was no material before any Court below to find that those are genuine signatures. The lower appellate Court compared the disputed signatures of Amulya Prasad in solenama, Exhibit B, and in vokalatnama, Exhibit C in the earlier suit with the admitted signature of the present plaint and found the same to be of different hands. Apart from this comparison, the lower appellate Court also considered the oral evidence on record to find out the genuineness of the alleged solenama. The lower appellate Court in this regard considered the testimony of the defendant's witnesses namely, D.Ws. 4 and 5 who were the clerks of the Advocates in the earlier suit. D.W.4 deposed that he wrote the solenama Exhibit B and D.W.5 deposed that he wrote the vokalatnama, Exhibit Court behalf of defendant No. 1 (Amulya Prashad) of Title Suit No. 101 of 1974. Both these witnesses in their cross-examination admitted that the parties did not sign the solenama in their presence but they signed the same in presence of their respective lawyers. The lawyers who conducted Title Suit No. 101 of 1974 were not also examined in this case. Defendant No. 1, SK. Ansaruddin, only deposed that Amulya signed the vokalatunama and the solenama in Title Suit No. 101 of 1974. D.W.1 being himself interested in the suit, the learned lower appellate Court thought it fit and proper not to believe the testimony of D.W.1. Thus apart from comparison of the disputed signatures, the appellate court on consideration of the oral evidence on record came to a finding of fact as to the genuineness of the solanama in the earlier suit. This being a pure finding of fact, the learned Single Judge committed an illegality in revision to set aside this finding. 

 10. It may be mentioned here that apart from the above finding, the lower appellate Court had also given other cogent reasons for setting aside the earlier decree to which the learned single Judge of the High Court Division was totally oblivious. The lower appellate Court found from perusal of the record that in the earlier suit there is nothing to show that summons and notices were served upon the defendant of that suit, but rather those were suppressed. It appears from the appellate Judgment that the learned Munsif did not rely on the service return of summons, that is why he ordered for issuing of fresh notices under a registered post and the appellate Court found from the record of that case that actually no notice was sent from the Court and neither the postal receipt, nor acknowledgement due was there in the records of the case and there was no endorsement in the order sheet that the registered post was actually sent. Further, the appellate Court found from the evidence of defendant himself of the present suit that notice under registered post was not sent in the earlier suit. Thus, the lower appellate Court found that there was suppression of summons and notices. The lower appellate Court further found on consideration of the Materials on record that the learned Munsif, in order to ascertain the truth of otherwise of the solenama, fixed the case on 20.3.1975 for hearing of the solenama but without ascertaining the truth of the solenama he passed the ex-parte decree on the basis of solenama. This is the most material finding of the lower appellate Court with regard to the suppression of the processes on the defendant of that suit and filing of a collusive and fraudulent solenama and obtaining of a compromise decree. This material finding with regard to the suppression of processes having been accepted by the learned single Judge of the High Court Division, the Judgment of the appellate Court ought not to have been set aside merely on the ground that the comparison of signatures by the Court of appeal below is wrong and hazadrous. Further, the lower appellate Court found from the materials on record that in Enemy Property Case No. XII-16/68-69 dated 15.3.76 the husband of the plaintiff filed a petition against leasing out of some lands to the present defendant as the land belonged to his two other brothers. In that proceeding, Amullya Prashad claimed that he was in possession of his own share and prayed for leasing out the shares of his two enemy brothers. In that preceding the present defendant Sk. Ansaruddin was a party and he did not assert that he had already purchased the share of Amulya or that he has got a "sole-decree" on 19.5.75. The appellate Court also found that this defendant wanted to suppress the existence of "sole-decree" to the A.D.C. or to anybody else before the filing of the present suit. Further, the Bainapatra which is the basis of the decree of the earlier suit was not taken into evidence at the time of disposal of that suit. During the trial of the present suit also the Bainapatra was not properly proved or taken into evidence as the scribe and the attesting witnesses of the Baniapatra were not examined. P.W.5 was examined as an attesting witness of the bainapatra but he denied to have attested the same. Hence, the lower appellate Court found that the decree holder of Title Suit No. 101 of 1974 got a decree by suppression of summons and by filing a collusive and fraudulent solenama.
